title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.2.0-preview.5
summary: Adds an optional administrator-launch setting for this Windows account and exact EXE location; new copies continue to run normally by default.
changes: Settings > Installation adds Run as administrator and displays the actual permissions of the current process separately from the next-launch choice.
The local choice defaults off and is stored per current Windows user and exact EXE path, outside portable pairing preferences.
An opted-in ordinary launch requests the Windows UAC approval for only its own EXE, with no forwarded arguments. Cancellation or startup errors leave the ordinary copy running.
Clipboard, installer, updater and validated secure-desktop modes retain their existing routing and tokens; the service and Windows UAC policy are unchanged.
The existing Start with Windows choice remains independent. No scheduled elevated task or RUNASADMIN compatibility override is created.
testing: Release x64 build and single-file publish passed; 125 focused elevation, UI and updater tests plus 65 existing regressions passed locally on Windows.
The administrator controls were rendered and visually inspected at normal and larger text sizes.
Finish transfers and exit MWB before a manual EXE replacement; keep adjacent preferences and recovery files. A same-path update preserves the local administrator-launch choice.
See docs/ADMIN_LAUNCH.md for exact real-UAC, peer-input, startup and clipboard validation limits.
known_limitations: Unsigned Windows x64 preview. Administrator mode elevates the whole ordinary application, including input received from peers; it is an explicit local opt-in.
Windows approval is still required. Cancelling UAC continues without administrator privileges, and already-running processes are not demoted by clearing the checkbox.
Explorer drag/drop, clipboard and file-transfer behavior across integrity levels require real-PC verification. Sign-in startup has not been established by a live logoff/logon test.
Protected UAC and sign-in input still use the separate optional service. Existing updater path restrictions and inherited full-suite failures remain documented.
